$comment: Locators whose verdict both parsers must agree on.
The `cheers:` grammar is implemented twice — in Rust by
frontend/src/features/chat/locator.ts — because agents write locators into text the
Gateway reads, and users click locators the browser resolves. Neither side can
Two hand-written parsers drift. These are the cases that must not: the shapes that
carry traversal, the fragments that are not anchors, and the five other meanings of
`cheers:` already in this codebase (OAuth scopes, the resource guide, the desktop
callback, a task-claim namespace string, a LiveKit identity).
`resource`/`params` are present only for locators that resolve to a read. A locator
may legitimately parse and still not resolve — see `unresolvable`.

cases.why: A picked passage becomes an explicit line window the agent resolves on demand.
A single line is a one-line window, not an open-ended one.
Tolerant on intent: a reversed range names the same lines.
A bot's real workspace file, addressed by handle.
A channel projection is addressed by the channel alone — no tail.
As above; the verb is channel.usage.read, not channel.cost.read.
Parses and navigates, but no read resource takes a message id — by-seq takes a seq window. Resolving it would mean a lookup inside a pure translation, or changing a shipped format.
Dot-segments never appear in an honest locator.
Backslashes are not path separators here.
A locator is a single token; whitespace means it is something else.
A fragment that is not a line anchor makes the whole locator malformed.
A kind that needs a tail, without one.
A channel projection takes no tail.
A message id has no path.
An OAuth scope, not a locator — the scheme is shared.
The resource guide URI: an authority form, not a locator.
A task-claim namespace string fed to Uuid::new_v5.
